heading: About
body: I own architecture and performance on large codebases, and run the code review that keeps them maintainable. Most of what I build is infrastructure other people build on: low-code platforms, back-office systems, document management, e-commerce. React, Next.js and TypeScript on the front, Node.js and PostgreSQL behind it, with LLM features in the recent products.

language.short: Designed the DSL behind a low-code reporting platform, so analysts could write their own formulas instead of filing tickets.
language.detail: Grammar, editor and evaluation: a parser built with Chevrotain and Lezer, wired into a CodeMirror 6 editor with completion and inline errors.

clients.short: Worked directly with clients in the EU and the US, with no manager in between.
clients.detail: Mostly contract work, straight with the client rather than through a delivery layer: agreeing what should be built before building it, then carrying the result to production.

platform.short: Owned the frontend architecture of that platform: a widget system configured at runtime.
platform.detail: Every table, chart and text block is defined by the user, over data read from their own databases, with undo/redo, archive creation and PDF export on top.

payments.short: Built payments and subscriptions from the store receipt through to the renewal job.
payments.detail: Receipt verification, webhooks, background jobs for renewal and expiry, and PostgreSQL access rules with logging that never writes a token. The part that has to be right the first time.

ai.short: Took LLM features from prototype to production, inside real product flows rather than a demo chat.
ai.detail: Retrieval over the product's own documents, streaming responses, tool calling and agent-style flows, routed through OpenRouter rather than tied to a single vendor.

performance.short: Kept large tables and charts responsive on codebases that had outgrown any one person's head.
performance.detail: Virtualised the big tables, split and lazy-loaded the routes, trimmed the bundle, and cut repeat GraphQL round trips with Apollo fragments and cache policies.

review.short: Set up the code review process, and mentored the developers who joined after.
review.detail: Wrote the specs the code was built from, and the shared AI coding rules and prompts the team worked to.

personal: I have worked with German, American, Israeli and Ukrainian teams, and most of my career has been remote, across timezones, with colleagues I have only ever met on a call. The same sentence carries different weight depending on who says it: direct feedback that is ordinary in one team reads as rudeness in another. Erin Meyer's «The Culture Map» is good on this. Knowing it removes a lot of friction that has nothing to do with the work.

I play the Dark Souls series. It teaches you to understand rather than to push harder: you get through a difficult place once you know how it works. Bugs are the same, guessing rarely gets you there and careful reading does.
I read manga, walk a lot, and make tea. Tea, incidentally, is the only skill on my LinkedIn that was endorsed without me asking.
